Finding a river plume from space, and clearing up murky water

Davina Whata, Michigan Technological University, September 2026

  1. Sentinel-2 imagery from the Copernicus Data Space (sentinelhub)
  2. Plume mask for the Ontonagon River mouth, Lake Superior
  3. Underwater image enhancement
###Davina Tashinga Whata

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from PIL import Image
from sentinelhub import (
    SHConfig, BBox, CRS, DataCollection, MimeType,
    SentinelHubRequest, bbox_to_dimensions, SentinelHubCatalog
)

config = SHConfig()
config.sh_client_id = "YOUR_CLIENT_ID"
with open("COPERNICUS_SECRET", "r") as f:
    config.sh_client_secret = f.read().strip()
config.sh_base_url = 'https://sh.dataspace.copernicus.eu'
config.sh_token_url = 'https://identity.dataspace.copernicus.eu/auth/realms/CDSE/protocol/openid-connect/token'

# Image 1: Ontonagon River mouth, true color (RGB) 

bbox1 = BBox((-89.39, 46.84, -89.28, 46.92), crs=CRS.WGS84)
resolution1 = 10  # metres
size1 = bbox_to_dimensions(bbox1, resolution=resolution1)
print(f"Image 1 resolution: {resolution1} m, dimensions: {size1} px")

date1 = "2026-09-02"

evalscript_rgb = """
//VERSION=3
function setup() {
  return {
    input: ["B02", "B03", "B04"],
    output: {bands: 3}
  };
}
function evaluatePixel(sample) {
  return [sample.B04, sample.B03, sample.B02];
}
"""

request1 = SentinelHubRequest(
    evalscript=evalscript_rgb,
    input_data=[
        SentinelHubRequest.input_data(
            DataCollection.SENTINEL2_L1C.define_from("s2l1c", service_url=config.sh_base_url),
            time_interval=(date1, date1),
        )
    ],
    responses=[SentinelHubRequest.output_response("default", MimeType.PNG)],
    bbox=bbox1,
    size=size1,
    config=config,
)

imgs1 = request1.get_data()
scaled_img1 = np.clip(imgs1[0] * 2.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
plt.imshow(scaled_img1)
plt.title(f"Ontonagon River mouth, true color (B04-B03-B02), {date1}")
plt.show()

Image.fromarray(scaled_img1).save("ontonagon_river_mouth.png")
print("Saved ontonagon_river_mouth.png")

Image 1 resolution: 10 m, dimensions: (865, 864) px

Saved ontonagon_river_mouth.png

2. Plume mask

from skimage import morphology, measure
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.patches as patches

img = scaled_img1.astype(float)
r, g, b = img[..., 0], img[..., 1], img[..., 2]
total = r + g + b + 1e-6
blue_fraction = b / total
brightness = img.mean(axis=2)

# Sample regions (row0, row1, col0, col1)
clear_water_box = (30, 130, 30, 200)
plume_box       = (240, 340, 380, 520)
nearshore_box   = (260, 300, 750, 800)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 8))
ax.imshow(scaled_img1)
for (r0, r1, c0, c1), color, label in [
    (clear_water_box, "cyan", "clear water"),
    (plume_box, "red", "plume"),
    (nearshore_box, "yellow", "nearshore fringe"),
]:
    ax.add_patch(patches.Rectangle((c0, r0), c1 - c0, r1 - r0,
                                    fill=False, edgecolor=color, linewidth=2))
    ax.text(c0, r0 - 5, label, color=color, fontsize=9, weight="bold")
ax.set_title("Sample regions used for the plume mask rule")
plt.show()

def report(name, r0, r1, c0, c1):
    patch = img[r0:r1, c0:c1].reshape(-1, 3)
    r_m, g_m, b_m = patch.mean(axis=0)
    bf = b_m / (r_m + g_m + b_m)
    print(f"{name:18s} R:{r_m:5.1f}  G:{g_m:5.1f}  B:{b_m:5.1f}  "
          f"blue_fraction:{bf:.2f}  brightness:{(r_m+g_m+b_m)/3:5.1f}")

report("Clear water", *clear_water_box)
report("Plume", *plume_box)
report("Nearshore fringe", *nearshore_box)

roi_row0, roi_row1, roi_col0, roi_col1 = 150, 430, 250, 650
roi_mask = np.zeros(brightness.shape, dtype=bool)
roi_mask[roi_row0:roi_row1, roi_col0:roi_col1] = True

water_mask = blue_fraction > 0.47
plume_candidates = water_mask & (brightness > 31.5) & roi_mask

land_mask = ~water_mask
shoreline_buffer = morphology.dilation(land_mask, morphology.disk(18))
plume_mask_raw = plume_candidates & ~shoreline_buffer

# Dilate-erode-dilate to close gaps and remove small speckle
plume_mask_clean = morphology.dilation(plume_mask_raw, morphology.disk(3))
plume_mask_clean = morphology.erosion(plume_mask_clean, morphology.disk(5))
plume_mask_clean = morphology.dilation(plume_mask_clean, morphology.disk(3))

labeled = measure.label(plume_mask_clean)
if labeled.max() > 0:
    largest_label = np.argmax(np.bincount(labeled.flat)[1:]) + 1
    plume_mask_final = labeled == largest_label
else:
    plume_mask_final = plume_mask_clean

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(18, 5))
axes[0].imshow(scaled_img1); axes[0].set_title("Original")
axes[1].imshow(plume_candidates, cmap="gray"); axes[1].set_title("Candidates (within ROI)")
axes[2].imshow(plume_mask_raw, cmap="gray"); axes[2].set_title("After shoreline exclusion")
axes[3].imshow(plume_mask_final, cmap="gray"); axes[3].set_title("Cleaned + largest region only")
for ax in axes: ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("plume_mask_stages.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

#  Final overlay figure 
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 8))
ax.imshow(scaled_img1)
overlay = np.zeros((*plume_mask_final.shape, 4))
overlay[plume_mask_final] = [1, 0, 0, 0.5]
ax.imshow(overlay)
ax.set_title("Final plume mask overlaid on original image")
plt.savefig("plume_mask_overlay.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

Plume              R: 15.9  G: 32.1  B: 49.7  blue_fraction:0.51  brightness: 32.6

### 3. Underwater image enhancement

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import cv2


files = ['bottom_image_1.png', 'bottom_image_2.png', 'bottom_image_3.png', 'bottom_image_4.png']
fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(12, 16))
for i, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert('RGB')
    arr = np.array(im)
    small = arr[::4, ::4, :]  # downsample for speed

    axes[i, 0].imshow(small)
    axes[i, 0].set_title(f)
    axes[i, 0].axis('off')

    for c, color in enumerate(['red', 'green', 'blue']):
        hist, bins = np.histogram(small[:, :, c].flatten(), bins=256, range=(0, 255))
        axes[i, 1].plot(bins[:-1], hist, color=color, alpha=0.8)
    axes[i, 1].set_title(f'{f} - RGB histogram')
    axes[i, 1].set_xlim(0, 255)

    means = small.reshape(-1, 3).mean(axis=0)
    print(f'{f}: mean R={means[0]:.1f}  G={means[1]:.1f}  B={means[2]:.1f}')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('q3_histograms_all4.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

bottom_image_1.png: mean R=37.3  G=68.1  B=10.1
bottom_image_2.png: mean R=153.0  G=152.2  B=163.9
bottom_image_3.png: mean R=187.6  G=214.1  B=50.5
bottom_image_4.png: mean R=6.3  G=25.8  B=8.0

def auto_gamma(arr):
    """Pick gamma so the mean brightness lands near mid-gray (128/255)."""
    mean_norm = arr.mean() / 255.0
    gamma = np.log(0.5) / np.log(mean_norm + 1e-6)
    return np.clip(gamma, 0.2, 5.0)

def apply_gamma(arr, gamma):
    normed = arr / 255.0
    corrected = np.power(normed, gamma)
    return np.clip(corrected * 255, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

def hist_eq_per_channel(arr):
    out = np.zeros_like(arr)
    for c in range(3):
        out[:, :, c] = cv2.equalizeHist(arr[:, :, c])
    return out

fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 3, figsize=(14, 16))
for i, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert('RGB')
    arr = np.array(im)
    small = arr[::3, ::3, :]

    g = auto_gamma(small)
    gamma_img = apply_gamma(small, g)
    eq_img = hist_eq_per_channel(small)

    axes[i, 0].imshow(small); axes[i, 0].set_title(f'{f}\nOriginal'); axes[i, 0].axis('off')
    axes[i, 1].imshow(gamma_img); axes[i, 1].set_title(f'Gamma corrected (g={g:.2f})'); axes[i, 1].axis('off')
    axes[i, 2].imshow(eq_img); axes[i, 2].set_title('Hist. equalized (per channel)'); axes[i, 2].axis('off')
    print(f, 'gamma=', round(g, 2))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('q3_gamma_histeq_compare.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

bottom_image_1.png gamma= 0.37
bottom_image_2.png gamma= 1.42
bottom_image_3.png gamma= 1.32
bottom_image_4.png gamma= 0.24

def lab_L_eq(arr):
    """Equalize only the Lightness channel in LAB space, leaving color untouched."""
    lab = cv2.cvtColor(arr, cv2.COLOR_RGB2LAB)
    l, a, b = cv2.split(lab)
    l_eq = cv2.equalizeHist(l)
    lab_eq = cv2.merge([l_eq, a, b])
    return cv2.cvtColor(lab_eq, cv2.COLOR_LAB2RGB)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 3, figsize=(14, 16))
for i, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert('RGB')
    arr = np.array(im)
    small = arr[::3, ::3, :]

    rgb_eq = hist_eq_per_channel(small)
    lab_eq = lab_L_eq(small)

    axes[i, 0].imshow(small); axes[i, 0].set_title(f'{f}\nOriginal'); axes[i, 0].axis('off')
    axes[i, 1].imshow(rgb_eq); axes[i, 1].set_title('RGB per-channel eq'); axes[i, 1].axis('off')
    axes[i, 2].imshow(lab_eq); axes[i, 2].set_title('LAB: equalize L only'); axes[i, 2].axis('off')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('q3_lab_compare.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

def unsharp_mask(arr, sigma=2, strength=1.5):
    blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(arr, (0, 0), sigma)
    sharpened = cv2.addWeighted(arr, 1 + strength, blurred, -strength, 0)
    return np.clip(sharpened, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 4, figsize=(18, 16))
for i, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert('RGB')
    arr = np.array(im)
    small = arr[::3, ::3, :]

    base = lab_L_eq(small)  # start from the LAB-equalized result

    bilateral = cv2.bilateralFilter(base, d=9, sigmaColor=75, sigmaSpace=75)
    median = cv2.medianBlur(base, 5)
    sharpened = unsharp_mask(bilateral, sigma=2, strength=1.2)

    axes[i, 0].imshow(base); axes[i, 0].set_title(f'{f}\nLAB-eq (base)'); axes[i, 0].axis('off')
    axes[i, 1].imshow(bilateral); axes[i, 1].set_title('Bilateral filter'); axes[i, 1].axis('off')
    axes[i, 2].imshow(median); axes[i, 2].set_title('Median filter'); axes[i, 2].axis('off')
    axes[i, 3].imshow(sharpened); axes[i, 3].set_title('Bilateral + unsharp mask'); axes[i, 3].axis('off')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('q3_smoothing_compare.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

Test image: applying the final pipeline

im = Image.open('bottom_image_contest.png').convert('RGB')
arr = np.array(im)
small = arr[::2, ::2, :]  #  good resolution 

base = lab_L_eq(small)
median = cv2.medianBlur(base, 5)
bilateral = cv2.bilateralFilter(median, d=9, sigmaColor=75, sigmaSpace=75)
final = unsharp_mask(bilateral, sigma=2, strength=1.2)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(20, 6))
axes[0].imshow(small); axes[0].set_title('Original'); axes[0].axis('off')
axes[1].imshow(base); axes[1].set_title('LAB L-equalized'); axes[1].axis('off')
axes[2].imshow(median); axes[2].set_title('+ median filter'); axes[2].axis('off')
axes[3].imshow(final); axes[3].set_title('+ bilateral + unsharp (final)'); axes[3].axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('contest_pipeline_stages.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

Image.fromarray(final).save('bottom_image_contest_enhanced.png')
print("Saved bottom_image_contest_enhanced.png")
